subject.title: [Feature]: Use Codex OAuth for browser realtime Talk

question: Should OpenClaw officially support a separate experimental Codex-OAuth browser Talk route that uses the Codex app-server rather than the documented OpenAI Platform API-key realtime path?
rationale: This changes the supported authentication and billing boundary for browser realtime voice, adds configuration, and depends on an upstream app-server protocol; source inspection alone cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental broker
options.body: Accept the new explicit mode, with a documented support boundary and focused review of token containment, app-server protocol use, cleanup, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep Platform API-key realtime only
options.body: Retain the existing documented public Realtime contract and close or narrow the paired PR as unsupported product direction.

options.title: Request a narrower contract proposal
options.body: Ask for a design that reuses an existing provider/auth seam without exposing a new browser Talk authentication mode.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental broker
recommendation.body: Accept the new explicit mode, with a documented support boundary and focused review of token containment, app-server protocol use, cleanup, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the paired implementation and can clarify the proposed protocol and proof while a repository owner makes the product decision.
